1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Quillon Cloud runs Tarnfield, a fictional object storage service. Stateless gateways terminate client requests, check request signatures, look up metadata and fetch object chunks from storage nodes. The fleet is organised as 12 cells across three regions (us-e, ap-s, eu-w). Gateway software ships through a release pipeline that posts to a shared change calendar. Storage-node settings are changed through a separate fleet configuration system.
9	Your request: The VP of Platform Engineering wants a decision today on rolling gateway 5.8 back to 5.7 across the fleet. You have been asked to assess what is driving the GET latency regression and which of the proposed actions should be taken. You may collect at most two items from the catalogue.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Priya Halvorsen, VP Platform Engineering, email to incident channel, 4 Nov 09:12 (leadership-account): GET p99 has been stuck near 300 ms since the gateway 5.8 rollout on the night of 2–3 Nov. Before that it was 90 ms. The dashboard shows it climbing as the rollout went out. 5.8 changed the read path, and gateway CPU is up 18%. I want a fleet-wide rollback to 5.7 today. Security has objected because of the signature fix, but customer latency comes first and we can re-ship the fix later. The storage and network teams have confirmed nothing of theirs is involved.
12	- Fleet latency dashboard export with deployment annotations (telemetry): Fleet GET p99, hourly average of 5-minute p99 values (ms), night of 2–3 Nov. Annotation: 'gateway 5.8 rollout 22:05–04:10 (us-e 22:05–23:30, ap-s 23:35–01:50, eu-w 02:30–04:10)'. 20:00 90; 21:00 91; 22:00 93; 23:00 139; 00:00 284; 01:00 291; 02:00 296; 03:00 301; 04:00 298; 05:00 297. Daily median p99: 1 Nov 90, 2 Nov 91, 4 Nov 296, 6 Nov 294, 8 Nov 297. The shared change calendar for 2–3 Nov has one entry: gateway 5.8 rollout.
13	- Gateway 5.8 release notes (approved 30 Oct) (change-record): Changes: (1) Fixes SEC-2291, a request-signature replay weakness reported by external auditors. Versions 5.7 and earlier remain exposed, and audit closure requires 5.8 across the fleet by 30 Nov. (2) Read path: parallel range-fetch fan-out raised from 4 to 8 for large objects. (3) TLS library upgrade. Known effect: gateway CPU +15–20% from the added signature checks. Rollback procedure: redeploy 5.7, about 4 hours across the fleet.
14	- Interview notes, storage platform manager, 4 Nov (manager-account): 'We pushed a routine compaction tuning change through the fleet config system on the evening of 2 Nov, because backlog alerts had been firing since about 31 Oct. Fleet config pushes don't go on the shared change calendar and never have. Compaction is background work and yields to client reads, so it can't be behind a read-latency problem. And to be clear, we never pause compaction. Once backlog passes about 15% of extents, read amplification climbs and nodes start running toward disk-full.'
15	- Network on-call handover note, 3 Nov 08:00 (staff-account): 'Elevated TCP retransmits on us-e spine-2 from 02:10 to 04:50 on 3 Nov, traced to a flapping optic. We replaced the optic at 04:50 and retransmits have been at baseline since. Nothing comparable in ap-s or eu-w. Gateway-to-storage round-trip time medians are 0.4–0.6 ms in all three regions, same as last week. We don't see a network angle on the GET latency issue.'
16	- Customer success note and traffic summary, 4 Nov (document): On 30 Oct Orrin Media began migrating its archive into Tarnfield, writing about 18 TB/day across all three regions. It is a background copy with a 15 Dec deadline and is currently ahead of schedule. Orrin's contract allows temporary ingest rate limits with 24 hours' notice, and their technical lead has said pacing is fine. Fleet traffic, 28 Oct to 4 Nov: GET requests/s rose 6%, gradually across the week. PUT requests/s rose 14%.
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	The latency jump is not caused by gateway 5.8. It was caused by the storage compaction tuning change pushed on the evening of 2 Nov. Evidence: in 11 cells the push raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Disk use went from 41% to 97% within minutes, and node-side GET time went from 61 ms to 262 ms. Each cell's latency jumped within about 5–10 minutes of its own push, regardless of when 5.8 arrived. Cell aps-3 received 5.8 but skipped the push, and its latency stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. The network is clean. A fleet-wide rollback would not fix latency and would reopen the security flaw, which has a 30 Nov audit deadline. Do not pause compaction. Instead, revert the tuning in one cell first and watch GET p99 and backlog, then extend to the other cells. Compaction is still needed, since backlog is 4.0% now and the 15% danger point is not expected before 13 Nov. Hold off on limiting Orrin until the 10 Nov attribution report. Confidence is high, and the one-cell revert is the cheap confirming test.
20
